entities.summary:
Twosret was the last known ruler and final pharaoh of the Nineteenth Dynasty of Egypt, reigning from circa 1188 to 1175 BCE. Born into a life of royalty, Twosret ascended to the throne following the death of her husband Pharaoh Seti II, whose reign she had co-ruled with him since 1191 BCE. During her rule, Twosret sought to legitimize her position by promoting herself as a divine ruler, often in conjunction with the powerful priestly class.

Twosret's reign was marked by significant political upheaval and military campaigns against neighboring regions, including Nubia and Syria. Her diplomatic endeavors aimed to strengthen Egypt's borders and secure its economic interests. The reign of Twosret also saw a renewed focus on the construction of temples and monuments in her honor, showcasing her ambition to leave a lasting legacy.

Twosret's decision to ascend to the throne without her husband led to controversy among Egyptian nobles and priests, who questioned her right to rule based on her sex. However, Twosret successfully navigated these challenges through strategic alliances with powerful figures and her own diplomatic prowess.

Twosret's reign ultimately came to an end when she was succeeded by her stepson Ramses III, but the impact of her legacy can still be seen in the architectural achievements and cultural artifacts left behind during her time on the throne.

'The gods have chosen me,' Twosret proclaimed, solidifying her place as one of Egypt's most fascinating and influential female pharaohs in history.
